notes: With the skill, 88 of 89 checks passed; without it, 76 of 89. The biggest gains: due dates worked out from the send date (the baseline guessed 'Wed Mar 18' for 'get back to you' and gave no dates for soft promises), stated-vs-guessed labels on dates, days-quiet counted from the user's last nudge, and asking for one view returning only that view.

Six cases passed in both setups (urgent, combined views, 7-day window, drafts, Telegram, no source), so they don't show what the skill adds. They need stricter checks, such as Ravi's rubric being due now, Chloe's proposal not being urgent, and the NDA, room booking and cc'd promise being left out.

A repeated skill error: three runs promoted the phone call with Sam to Done on the strength of 'as discussed'. The skill should keep promises kept off email (calls, in person) at 'probably done' unless the other person confirms.

Smaller skill errors: a request that was asked and answered (Ivy's room booking) was counted as a closed promise; in the Needed view, an ASAP request and Ravi's rubric (due today, guessed date) were sorted after items due weeks later; the full report's 'this week' bucket included an item due Mar 31; 'last 5 days' was read as Mar 8-13, which is 6 days counting both ends.
A design question: on a later run the skill only scans from the last scan date, so open items an earlier scan missed (Alex's approval, the expense report) never get picked up.
Cost: the skill took about 38 seconds and 9,000 tokens more per run on average, mostly reading the skill and writing the tracker file.
